mainTopic: The garments and status of the משוח מלחמה, and how the אורים ותומים is consulted.
overview: On the previous amud, רב דימי reported in רבי יוחנן's name that the משוח מלחמה does the עבודה in the eight garments of a כהן גדול. The גמרא tests this claim against several ברייתות. To the first one, רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the son inherits only a position whose main purpose is the אוהל מועד, and the משוח מלחמה's anointing is mainly for war. To the second, which says he wears neither four nor eight garments, אביי answers that he does not wear eight because of איבה, and he cannot drop to four because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. רב אדא בר אבא then brings a long ברייתא listing the differences between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט, and argues that its תנא ignores איבה. The גמרא replies that איבה is felt only toward someone lower in rank, not toward an equal. Next comes a story in which רבי אמי and רבי אסי silently showed disagreement with this teaching. רבין then reports a different version: the משוח מלחמה wears the eight garments only when he is consulted through the אורים ותומים, and a ברייתא supports this. The amud ends with how the אורים ותומים is consulted: where each person faces, what they say, speaking quietly like חנה, and asking only one question at a time. The answer to the question about דוד's two questions continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The פסוק limits inheritance to one fit to enter the אוהל מועד
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: the son inherits only the anointed position of a כהן who is fit to enter the אוהל מועד. This leaves out the משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Seven days shall the כהן from his sons who serves in his place wear them, who will come into the אוהל מועד.' This means one who is fit to come into the אוהל מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. It uses a פסוק to show that only a כהן fit to enter the אוהל מועד passes his position to his son, so the son of a משוח מלחמה does not inherit. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'תחתיו מבניו' (his son in his place) teaches that the position is inherited. The added words 'אשר יבא אל אהל מועד' limit that rule to a כהן whose role involves the אוהל מועד. The ברייתא uses this limit to exclude the משוח מלחמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a source that settles a question)
His son in his place: the source that the anointed position is inherited
The Tent of Meeting, meaning the inner sanctuary
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before war

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a ברייתא. The 'one might think' part, which asked whether the son of the משוח מלחמה inherits, came just before.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Seven days shall the priest wear them,
the one in his stead from among his sons,
who will come into the Tent of Meeting"

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לָבֹא אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: meaning one who is fit to come into the Tent of Meeting.
phrases.notes: This excludes the משוח מלחמה from passing his position to his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud, which is brought to test רב דימי's claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a כהן fit to enter the אוהל מועד passes his anointed position to his son. The משוח מלחמה is excluded.

steps.title: If he wears eight garments, he should be fit to enter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב דימי: if the משוח מלחמה wears the eight garments of a כהן גדול, then he is fit to enter the אוהל מועד, and the ברייתא should not exclude him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so that he serves in eight garments, then he is indeed fit to enter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack רב דימי's statement that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing the eight garments of a כהן גדול would seem to make him fit for the inner עבודה. If so, the ברייתא's reason for excluding him, that he is not 'fit to enter the אוהל מועד', falls apart. So either רב דימי is wrong, or the ברייתא needs a different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (introduces a challenge to someone's claim)
He is certainly fit

phrases.english: And if it is so (that he serves in eight garments),
he is indeed fit (to enter the Tent of Meeting)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא in step 1 to challenge רב דימי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eight garments would make him fit to enter the אוהל מועד. That contradicts the ברייתא, which excludes him for being unfit.

steps.title: The פסוק means one whose anointing is mainly for the אוהל מועד
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the ברייתא differently. The point is not technical fitness to enter. It is the main purpose of the anointing, and the משוח מלחמה was anointed mainly for war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is what the ברייתא means: anyone whose anointing is mainly for the אוהל מועד. That leaves out this one, whose anointing is mainly for war.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by explaining what 'fit to enter the אוהל מועד' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that the משוח מלחמה is technically able to enter. However, the ברייתא is about why he was anointed in the first place. Since his anointing exists mainly for war, his son does not inherit it. That is fully consistent with רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (re-reads a source)
The main purpose of his anointing
This one is excluded

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
This is what it is saying:
Anyone whose anointing is primarily for the Tent of Meeting.
This one is excluded,
whose anointing is primarily for war.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Fit to enter' means technically allowed to serve inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Fit to enter' means anointed mainly for the אוהל מועד, which excludes the משוח מלחמה even though he wears eight garments.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates being allowed to do something from what a role is mainly for. Only the main purpose decides whether the son inherits.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he wears neither four nor eight garments
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to רב דימי: a ברייתא states that the משוח מלחמה serves neither in four garments like a regular כהן nor in eight like a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The משוח מלחמה does not serve in four garments like a כהן הדיוט, and not in eight like a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רב דימי's claim about eight garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי said the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments. This ברייתא says he does not. The contradiction looks direct.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, who serves in four garments
The High Priest, who serves in eight garments

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The priest anointed for war does not serve
neither in four garments like a common priest,
nor in eight like a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב דימי, from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says he does not serve in eight garments.

steps.title: אביי explains the two reasons behind the ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects reading the ברייתא literally, since that would make the משוח מלחמה like a זר. He explains that the ברייתא gives two separate reasons: he does not dress like a כהן גדול because of איבה, and he does not dress like a כהן הדיוט because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Would you make him like a זר? Rather, he does not dress like a כהן גדול because of איבה, and he does not dress like a כהן הדיוט because we raise people up in holiness and do not lower them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. The ברייתא is not saying the משוח מלחמה has no right to the eight garments. It explains why, in practice, he wears neither set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, a כהן who serves in no garments would be like a non-כהן, which makes no sense. So by Torah law he really does wear eight, just as רב דימי said. The rabbis held him back because of איבה, the bad feelings it could cause with the כהן גדול. He cannot be lowered to four garments because his holiness has already been raised.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Bad feelings, here between him and the כהן גדול
We raise people up in holiness and do not lower them
You would make him

steps.whatToRemember: The משוח מלחמה has the status of eight garments by Torah law, so רב דימי stands. In practice he wears neither set: not eight because of איבה, and not four because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Neither four nor eight' does not mean he is outside the category of an anointed כהן. It is a special rule about how his status is carried out in practice, and his eight-garment status remains.
steps.whyThisMatters: מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין is a general principle that appears throughout שס.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But then you would make him like a non-priest!
Rather: not like a High Priest, due to animosity;

phrases.aramaic: כְּכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט — מִשּׁוּם מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין.
phrases.english: not like a common priest, due to the principle that one elevates in sanctity and does not downgrade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא זָר מְשַׁוֵּית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא as a rabbinic limit, not a statement of his Torah-law status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא denies that the משוח מלחמה has any garment status.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law he wears eight. In practice he wears neither set, because of איבה and מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.

steps.title: A teacher who ignores animosity still keeps the war priest out of eight garments
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבא challenges רבא. There is a תנא who does not accept the איבה concern, and yet according to him the משוח מלחמה still does not serve in eight garments. So איבה cannot be the real reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבא said to רבא: But there is this תנא who does not accept the concern of איבה, and still the משוח מלחמה does not serve in eight garments.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רב אדא בר אבא says the איבה reason cannot explain everything, because one תנא does not hold of איבה and still keeps the משוח מלחמה out of the eight garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step explained that the משוח מלחמה does not wear the eight garments because it would cause איבה with the real כהן גדול. If some תנא rejects that worry entirely but reaches the same result, there must be a different reason. The proof comes from the ברייתא quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: Animosity or jealousy. Here, the worry that the כהן גדול would resent the משוח מלחמה dressing like him.
A sage of the משנה period. Here it means the author of a ברייתא.
Serves in the בית המקדש. Here it means serving while wearing the eight garments.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'וְלָא קָא מְשַׁמֵּשׁ' does not mean the משוח מלחמה never serves at all. It means he does not serve in the eight garments of a כהן גדול.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Abba said to Rava:
But this tanna, who does not hold of the concern of animosity,
and yet [the war priest] does not serve [in eight garments].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא: וְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the איבה reason given in step 5 for why the משוח מלחמה does not wear eight garments.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משוח מלחמה avoids the eight garments because of איבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא who rejects איבה still reaches the same ruling. So איבה cannot be the necessary reason, and a different reason must exist.

steps.title: The list of differences begins: קרבנות only a כהן גדול brings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists the differences between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט. It starts with the קרבנות that only a כהן גדול brings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: These are the matters that differ between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט. The פר כהן משיח, which is also called the bull brought for all the מצוות. The פר יום הכפורים. And the עשירית האיפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב אדא בר אבא's challenge. This step is setting up a long list, and the list continues over the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists what is unique to a כהן גדול compared with a regular כהן. The first item is a group of קרבנות that belong only to the כהן גדול. 'פר כהן משיח' and 'פר הבא על כל המצות' are two names for the same bull.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular, ordinary כהן who is not the כהן גדול.
The bull the anointed כהן גדול brings when he mistakenly rules and acts on a serious איסור.
A tenth of an איפה of flour. This is the daily מנחה the כהן גדול offers.
The special bull the כהן גדול offers on יום כפור.

steps.confusionAlert: 'פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ' and 'פַּר הַבָּא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת' are not two different bulls. They are one bull with two names.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט:
phrases.english: The matters that differ between a High Priest and a common priest:
the bull of the anointed priest,
which is the bull brought for [transgressing] any of the מצוות,
phrases.notes: This is the same bull as the previous phrase, described by its purpose.

phrases.english: and the bull of Yom Kippur,
and the tenth of an ephah [daily meal-offering].

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that step 6 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a תנא who rejects איבה still holds the משוח מלחמה does not serve in eight garments.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing the differences between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: The list continues: mourning, marriage, and the accidental killer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A כהן גדול does not let his hair grow or tear his clothes as a mourner normally does, except below. He does not become טמא for relatives. He must marry a בתולה and may not marry an אלמנה. His death lets the רוצח בשוגג go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול does not let his hair grow wild and does not tear his clothes. But he does tear from below, while the כהן הדיוט tears from above. He does not become טמא for his relatives. He is commanded to marry a בתולה, he is forbidden to marry an אלמנה, and his death sends the accidental killer home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא. These items cover personal rules where the כהן גדול is stricter or has a special role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן tears his garment at the top like any mourner, but a כהן גדול may only tear at the bottom, where it is not noticeable. A regular כהן may become טמא for close relatives and may marry an אלמנה, but a כהן גדול may not do either. The death of the כהן גדול frees the accidental killer from the עיר מקלט.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets the hair grow long and wild, as a mourner normally does.
Tears his clothing as a sign of mourning.
A widow. A כהן גדול may not marry her.
Lets the accidental killer return home. This happens when the כהן גדול dies.

phrases.english: He does not let his hair grow wild, and he does not rend [his garments],
but he does rend from below,
while the common priest [rends] from above.
And he does not become impure for his relatives,
and he is commanded [to marry] a virgin,
and he is prohibited from [marrying] a widow,
and [his death] returns the accidental killer.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא פּוֹרֵעַ, וְלֹא פּוֹרֵם, אֲבָל פּוֹרֵם הוּא מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the ברייתא of differences.

steps.title: The list ends: mourning service, priority, eight garments, and יום כפור
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends. A כהן גדול may offer קרבנות while he is an אונן but may not eat or share in them. He takes his portion first and offers first. He serves in eight garments. He is exempt from the קרבן for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. All of the עבודת יום הכפורים is valid only through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings קרבנות while an אונן, but he does not eat from them and does not take a share. He takes his portion first and offers first. He serves in eight garments. He is exempt for causing טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. And all the עבודות of יום כפור are valid only when he does them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. Notice that 'serves in eight garments' appears here as something that sets the כהן גדול apart. This item is what matters for the question about the משוח מלחמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן may not do עבודה on the first day of mourning, but a כהן גדול may, though he still may not eat the קרבן. The ברייתא lists 'eight garments' as a mark of the כהן גדול compared with the הדיוט, and the גמרא will use this to show the תנא's view on the משוח מלחמה. The ברייתא also gives the כהן גדול first choice of portions and offerings, an exemption from one קרבן, and sole charge of the יום כפור service.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the first day after a close relative dies, before the burial is fully behind him.
Taking first, with first choice of portions or of which קרבן to offer.
The eight garments of the כהן גדול. A regular כהן wears four.
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא. Others bring a קרבן for this, but the כהן גדול is exempt.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists 'מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּשְׁמֹנָה כֵּלִים' as a difference between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט. רב אדא בר אבא uses this ברייתא to show a תנא who keeps the משוח מלחמה out of the eight garments without relying on איבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key list of the unique laws of the כהן גדול. It is the base for the next move in the debate over whether איבה is the true reason the משוח מלחמה does not wear eight garments.

phrases.english: And he sacrifices [offerings] while an acute mourner,
but he does not eat and does not take a share,
and he takes his portion first,
and he offers first.
And he serves in eight garments,
and he is exempt [from an offering] for impurity of the Temple and its sacred items,
and all the services of Yom Kippur
are valid only through him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַקְרִיב אוֹנֵן, וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל, וְאֵינוֹ חוֹלֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 7, including the 'eight garments' item that matters for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 6 that this תנא keeps the משוח מלחמה out of the eight garments without relying on איבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's listing of 'מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּשְׁמֹנָה כֵּלִים' as a difference between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: All the laws apply to a כהן גדול of many garments (מרובה בגדים)
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that all of the כהן גדול laws apply to a כהן גדול who became כהן גדול by wearing the extra garments rather than by anointing oil. The one exception is the פר הבא על כל המצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these laws apply to a כהן גדול who was made one by wearing the many garments, except for the bull brought for all the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. After listing what makes a כהן גדול special, it now tells us which kinds of כהן גדול these laws apply to. This first line is about the מרובה בגדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second בית המקדש there was no anointing oil, so a כהן גדול was put into office by wearing the eight garments. The ברייתא says he is a full כהן גדול for almost everything. The one exception is the special bull for a mistaken ruling, because the תורה ties it to the 'anointed' כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them apply (all the laws just listed)
A כהן גדול made one by wearing the eight garments, not by anointing oil
The bull a כהן גדול brings for a mistaken ruling about any מצוה (פר כהן משיח)

phrases.english: And all of them apply to one of many garments,
phrases.notes: A כהן גדול put into office by wearing the eight garments

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפַּר הַבָּא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת.
phrases.english: except for the bull brought for all the commandments.
phrases.notes: This bull belongs only to an anointed כהן גדול

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 9 by applying its list to different types of כהן גדול.
steps.raayaObject: רב אדא בר אבא's challenge that איבה is not the reason
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing the differences between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט

steps.title: All the laws apply to a former כהן גדול (משוח שעבר)
steps.stepSummary: All the כהן גדול laws, including serving in eight garments, apply to a משוח שעבר. The exceptions are the פר יום הכפורים and the daily עשירית האיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these laws apply to a former כהן גדול, except for the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of an איפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says a substitute כהן גדול who stepped down keeps almost all the laws of a כהן גדול. This is the key line for רב אדא בר אבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list in step 9 included 'he serves in eight garments.' So the משוח שעבר also wears all eight garments, alongside the current כהן גדול. This means the תנא is not worried that the current כהן גדול will feel איבה toward someone dressed like him.

keyTerms.meaning: A former כהן גדול, a substitute who served while the regular one was disqualified and then stepped back
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול (חביתין)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mention the garments in this line. The proof comes from combining it with step 9: eight garments was one of the laws listed, and 'all of them apply' except two items. So the משוח שעבר wears eight garments.

phrases.english: And all of them apply to a former anointed priest,
phrases.notes: This includes serving in the eight garments

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה.
phrases.english: except for the bull of Yom Kippur and the tenth of an ephah.
phrases.notes: Only the כהן גדול now serving brings these

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next type of כהן גדול in the same ברייתא. This one gives the half of the proof that shows the תנא is not worried about איבה.
steps.raayaObject: That this תנא does not accept the איבה concern
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying the משוח שעבר keeps all the laws, including the eight garments

steps.title: The משוח מלחמה keeps only five laws
steps.stepSummary: None of the כהן גדול laws apply to the משוח מלחמה, except the five in the פרשה about mourning, טומאה and marriage. There is also a dispute about whether his death frees the accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And none of them apply to the משוח מלחמה, except five things said in the פרשה. He does not let his hair grow wild or tear his clothes. He does not become טמא for his relatives. He must marry a בתולה and may not marry an אלמנה. According to רבי יהודה his death also lets the רוצח go home, but the חכמים say it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by saying the משוח מלחמה gets almost none of the כהן גדול laws. That means he does not wear the eight garments. This completes רב אדא בר אבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same תנא who let the משוח שעבר wear eight garments without worrying about איבה. Yet he still denies the eight garments to the משוח מלחמה. So, says רב אדא בר אבא, איבה cannot be the reason the משוח מלחמה does not wear them.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן anointed to speak to the army before war
Lets his hair grow wild, as a mourner normally does
Tears his clothes, as a mourner normally does
The accidental killer living in an עיר מקלט

steps.whyThisMatters: The מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about the רוצח is discussed in מסכת מכות. Here it only shows how far the משוח מלחמה is treated like a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: And none of them apply to the priest anointed for war,
phrases.notes: So he does not wear the eight garments

phrases.english: except for five things stated in the passage:
phrases.notes: ויקרא כא, the פרשה of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: he does not let his hair grow wild, and does not tear his clothes,
phrases.notes: The normal mourning practices

phrases.english: and he does not become impure for his relatives,
and he is commanded to marry a virgin,
and he is warned against marrying a widow,
and his death returns the killer home,
phrases.notes: The accidental killer may leave the עיר מקלט

phrases.english: according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Sages say: he does not return him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא. Together with step 11 it completes רב אדא בר אבא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That איבה is not why the משוח מלחמה does not wear the eight garments
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא allows eight garments for the משוח שעבר but not for the משוח מלחמה

steps.title: No jealousy toward an equal, but jealousy toward someone lower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The תנא is not worried about איבה toward an equal like the משוח שעבר. He is worried about it toward someone lower in rank like the משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he has no jealousy, that is toward someone like himself. Toward someone lower than him, he does have jealousy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אדא בר אבא and saves the איבה reason that אביי gave in step 5. It shows that the ברייתא can fit with the איבה concern after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משוח שעבר was once a full כהן גדול, so seeing him in the same clothes does not bother the current כהן גדול. A משוח מלחמה was never on that level. Seeing a lower כהן dressed exactly like him would bother the כהן גדול. So the ברייתא does not prove that the תנא rejects איבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hostility or jealousy
Toward someone like him, of equal rank
Toward someone smaller (lower) than him

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's איבה reason from step 5 stands. The משוח מלחמה does not wear the eight garments because of איבה. The concern only applies to someone lower than the כהן גדול, so the משוח שעבר may wear them.

phrases.english: When he has no jealousy, that is toward someone like himself,
phrases.notes: Such as the משוח שעבר

phrases.english: toward someone lower than him, he does have it.
phrases.notes: Such as the משוח מלחמה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 10–12 and protects אביי's איבה reason from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that the תנא of the ברייתא rejects the איבה concern entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treated איבה as all or nothing. In fact, איבה applies only toward someone of lower rank, not toward an equal.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי turn their faces away
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו repeated רבי יוחנן's teaching that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away in silent disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו was sitting and saying this teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן. רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. When רבי אבהו repeated the teaching that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments, two great Sages showed they disagreed by turning their faces away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "This teaching" means רב דימי's report that, according to רבי יוחנן, the משוח מלחמה serves in all eight garments of the כהן גדול. רבי אמי and רבי אסי were students of רבי יוחנן. Turning their faces away was a silent way of saying: we do not believe רבי יוחנן said this.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling (here, רבי יוחנן's teaching about the משוח מלחמה)
They turned their faces away, a silent sign of disagreement

steps.confusionAlert: They did not argue out loud. Their disagreement was shown only by body language. This detail matters for רב פפא's question in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu was sitting
and saying this teaching
phrases.notes: The teaching that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.

phrases.aramaic: אַהְדְּרִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי לְאַפַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away.
phrases.notes: A silent sign that they disagreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב דימי's teaching in רבי יוחנן's name (that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments) and shows that רבי יוחנן's students doubted the report itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי silently disagreed when רבי אבהו reported in רבי יוחנן's name that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments.

steps.title: A second version: it was רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: Some say the teaching was repeated by רבי חייא בר אבא, not רבי אבהו, and that it was from him that רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי חייא בר אבא said it, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same story. In this version, the one repeating the teaching was רבי חייא בר אבא. This version sets up רב פפא's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silent disagreement is the same in both versions. Only the person who repeated the teaching changes. That detail will matter, because the reason for staying silent depends on who was speaking.

phrases.english: Some say,
Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַהְדְּרִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי לְאַפַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אֲמַרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the story in Step 14, with a different speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the second version, רבי חייא בר אבא repeated the teaching, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי silently disagreed.

steps.title: רב פפא: why would they stay silent to רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues against the second version. Silence fits only רבי אבהו, whom they respected because of his ties to the Roman government. To רבי חייא בר אבא they would have simply said that רבי יוחנן never said this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: It makes sense with רבי אבהו, because of the honor of the Caesar's house. But to רבי חייא בר אבא, they should have said outright: רבי יוחנן did not say this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the second version of the story. He argues that only the first version, with רבי אבהו, explains why they disagreed silently instead of speaking up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו was close to the Roman government, so the Sages showed him special respect and did not contradict him openly. רבי חייא בר אבא had no such status, so there was no reason to stay quiet. They would have just told him directly. Therefore the second version seems wrong, and the first version stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it
It makes sense with (the first case), but...
Respect for the house of Caesar (the Roman government)
Outright, openly in words

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
It makes sense if it was Rabbi Abahu
because of the honor of the Caesar's house,
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו had close ties to the Roman authorities, so they would not contradict him openly.

phrases.english: but to Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
they should have said to him outright:
Rabbi Yochanan did not say this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version saying רבי חייא בר אבא was the one who repeated the teaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Silent disagreement only makes sense if open disagreement was impossible. That was true only with רבי אבהו, because of his ties to the government. With רבי חייא בר אבא they would have spoken openly.

steps.title: רבין: the teaching was about being consulted
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן's teaching was really about the משוח מלחמה wearing the eight garments when he is consulted through the אורים ותומים, not about serving in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: It was stated about being consulted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין, coming from ארץ ישראל, gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's teaching. The eight garments are needed for being consulted, not for doing the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This disagrees with רב דימי's report that the משוח מלחמה serves in eight garments. In רבין's version, he wears the eight garments only when people ask him questions through the אורים ותומים, which sit in the חושן. He never does the Temple service in them. This also explains why רבי אמי and רבי אסי objected to רב דימי's version.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Being consulted (asked a question answered through the אורים ותומים)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up two different things. Serving (doing the עבודה) in the eight garments is one thing. Wearing them in order to be consulted is another. רבין says only the second applies to the משוח מלחמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's view, one that fits the silent objection of his students.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
It was stated about being consulted.
phrases.notes: He wears the eight garments only when consulted through the אורים ותומים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר: נִשְׁאַל אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different report of רבי יוחנן's teaching that fits the disagreement of רבי אמי and רבי אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משוח מלחמה wears the eight garments only when he is consulted, not to perform the עבודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the משוח מלחמה is consulted while wearing the garments in which the כהן גדול serves, supporting רבין's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: In the garments in which the כהן גדול serves, the משוח מלחמה is consulted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבין said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the משוח מלחמה is consulted in the כהן גדול's garments. It does not say he serves in them. This matches רבין's report that the eight garments are needed only for being consulted.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
The כהן anointed to lead the people in war

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין, supported by this ברייתא, the משוח מלחמה wears the eight garments only when he is consulted through the אורים ותומים, not for the עבודה. This differs from רב דימי's report that he serves in them.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
In the garments in which the High Priest serves
the priest anointed for war is consulted in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבין's statement in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבין's report that the eight-garment teaching is about being consulted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the משוח מלחמה is consulted in the garments in which the כהן גדול serves.

steps.title: How the אורים ותומים is consulted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the procedure. The person asking faces the כהן being asked, and the כהן faces the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: How does one consult? The one asking faces the one being asked, and the one being asked faces the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that explains how a question is asked through the אורים ותומים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person with the question stands facing the כהן. The כהן turns toward the שכינה. This means he looks toward the אורים ותומים in the חושן, which contain the name of הקב"ה, by bending his head down toward them.

keyTerms.meaning: How does one consult (the אורים ותומים)?
Toward, facing
The Divine Presence (here, the אורים ותומים with הקב"ה's name)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: How does one consult?
The one asking has his face toward the one being asked,
phrases.notes: The one being asked is the כהן גדול or the משוח מלחמה.

phrases.english: and the one being asked has his face toward the Divine Presence.
phrases.notes: He tilts his head down toward the אורים ותומים in the חושן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the משוח מלחמה is consulted in the eight garments, the גמרא explains how consulting works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one asking faces the כהן, and the כהן faces the שכינה (the אורים ותומים).

steps.title: What the asker says and what the כהן answers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives sample wording: the asker asks 'Shall I chase this troop?' and the כהן answers 'Thus says ה׳: Go up and succeed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The one asking says: 'Shall I chase after this troop?' And the one being asked says: 'Thus says ה׳: Go up and succeed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues describing the procedure for the אורים ותומים. It gives an example of the question and the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 told us where each person faces. Now we learn what each one says. The question comes from דוד's words in שמואל א׳ ל׳, and the כהן announces the answer as a message from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: The one asking (the king or leader)
The one being asked (the כהן wearing the אורים ותומים)
A troop or raiding band
Go up and succeed

phrases.english: The one asking says: 'Shall I pursue this troop?'
phrases.notes: Quoting דוד's question in שמואל א׳ ל:ח

phrases.english: And the one being asked says:
'Thus says God: Go up and succeed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא's description of the procedure, moving from body position to spoken words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן relays the answer with the opening 'כה אמר ה׳' followed by the content.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no need to say 'Thus says God'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds the כהן just says 'Go up and succeed' without the opening 'כה אמר ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He does not need to say 'Thus says God.' He just says 'Go up and succeed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the wording in the previous step. He says the opening phrase is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone already knows the כהן is only passing on what the אורים ותומים showed. So, according to רבי יהודה, it is enough to give the content of the answer. The disagreement is only about wording, not about how the process works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary
Thus says God (the opening formula of a prophetic message)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He need not say 'Thus says God,'
rather, just 'Go up and succeed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion inside the ברייתא about the answer's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The content alone ('עלה והצלח') is enough. The opening formula is not needed.

steps.title: The question is whispered, like חנה's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The question is not asked out loud and not just thought. It is said with the lips quietly, as חנה prayed. Each part is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not ask in a loud voice, because the פסוק says 'he shall ask for him' (only for himself). He also does not just think it in his heart, because the פסוק says 'he shall ask for him before ה׳'. Rather, he asks the way חנה spoke in her prayer, as it says: 'And חנה was speaking in her heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now teaches how loudly the question is asked. It sets two limits and gives the middle path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ושאל לו' means asking for himself, so others should not hear it, which rules out a loud voice. 'לפני ה׳' means it is a real spoken request, so pure thought is not enough. חנה moved her lips but made no sound, and that is the model.

keyTerms.meaning: Out loud, audibly
Thinks it only in his heart, without speaking
Mother of שמואל, whose silent lip-moving prayer is the model
Speaking in her heart (lips moving, voice not heard)

steps.whyThisMatters: This same model of חנה is the source for saying שמונה עשרה in a whisper.

phrases.english: One does not ask in a loud voice,
as it says: 'And he shall ask for him.'
phrases.notes: במדבר כז:כא, meaning asked for him alone

phrases.english: He does not just think it in his heart,
as it says: 'And he shall ask for him before God,'
rather, the way Hannah spoke in her prayer,
as it says: 'And Hannah was speaking in her heart.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ א:יג

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what is said to how loudly the asker says it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question is spoken quietly with the lips, not shouted and not only thought.

steps.title: Only one question at a time, and only the first is answered
steps.stepSummary: One may not ask two questions together. If someone does, only one is answered, and it is the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not ask two things at once. And if he did ask, they answer only one, and they answer him only the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a new rule about the number of questions. It also says what happens if someone breaks the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here. First, you are not supposed to ask two questions together. Second, if you did, you get only one answer, and it is to the first question. The second part is what the גמרא will challenge in a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Two matters at the same time
They answer (literally, they return a reply)
The first (question)

phrases.english: One does not ask about two matters at once.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שָׁאַל — אֵין מַחְזִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד,
phrases.english: And if he did ask, they answer only one,
and they answer him only the first,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another rule of the procedure, this time about how many questions may be asked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ask one question at a time. If two are asked, only the first is answered.

steps.title: Proof from דוד's two questions about קעילה
steps.stepSummary: דוד asked two questions, whether the people of קעילה would hand him over and whether שאול would come down. ה׳ answered only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Will the men of קעילה hand me over to him? Will שאול come down?' And ה׳ said: 'He will come down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove that only one answer is given when two questions are asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד asked two questions in one breath and got one answer. That supports 'only one is answered.' But the answer, 'he will come down,' is about the second question, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Will they hand me over?
The citizens of the town of קעילה
He will come down

phrases.english: as it says: 'Will the men of Keilah hand me over into his hand?
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ כג:יא

phrases.english: Will Saul come down?' etc.
And God said: 'He will come down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the rule in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only one of two questions is answered
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א׳ כג:יא, where דוד asked two questions and received one answer

steps.title: But דוד was answered on his second question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: you said only the first question is answered, yet דוד got an answer to his second question.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said they answer only the first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the proof seems to contradict the rule it was brought for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's first question was about קעילה and his second was about שאול. The answer 'ירד' is about שאול, the second question. So the פסוק supports 'only one answer' but seems to contradict 'only the first.'

keyTerms.meaning: But you said! (introduces a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against 'only one answer.' The פסוק fits that part. It is only against the claim that the answer goes to the first question.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ אֵין מַחְזִירִין אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן!
phrases.english: But didn't you say they answer only the first?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ אֵין מַחְזִירִין אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 24 using the rule in step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the very פסוק brought as proof, the answer given was to דוד's second question, not his first.

steps.title: The answer begins: דוד asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer by explaining how דוד actually asked. The answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד asked...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening words of the answer. The גמרא is setting up its explanation of how דוד asked, and the rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will focus on how דוד asked his questions, to show that he really did not break the rule. We need the next lines to see the full answer.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד asked

phrases.english: David asked
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: how דוד phrased his questions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד asked two questions properly and received an answer to the second, which would contradict the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet complete. The explanation of how דוד asked continues on the next amud.
